title: Add and subtract integers
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review

sections.title: Add two negatives
sections.objective: Add negative numbers by moving left on the number line.
explain: Owing $3 and then owing $5 more means you owe $8: that's −8, not 8.
sections.key: Adding a negative moves left. Both negative: add the sizes and keep the negative sign.

sections.title: Add a positive and a negative
explain: They partly cancel, so the answer is closer to 0 than the bigger number.
sections.key: Different signs: subtract the sizes, and keep the sign of the number with the bigger size.

worked.note: −7 has the bigger size, so the answer is negative.

sections.title: Subtract by adding the opposite
sections.objective: Change subtraction into adding the opposite, then add.
explain: Taking away a debt of $6 leaves you $6 better off: 4 − (−6) = 10.
sections.key: Subtracting is adding the opposite. Keep the first number, change − to +, change the sign of the second.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.objective: Add and subtract integers, mixed together.
sections.key: Subtracting? Change it to adding the opposite first. Then: same signs, add the sizes; different signs, subtract the sizes and keep the bigger one's sign.

hints.int.add-sub.same-sign: Both numbers are negative: start at the first one and move left. Add the sizes and keep the negative sign.
hints.int.add-sub.different-signs: Subtract the sizes, then use the sign of the number with the bigger size.
hints.int.add-sub.subtract: Change − to + and change the sign of the second number. Then add.
hints.int.add-sub: Subtracting? Add the opposite first. Then use the sign rules for adding.

misconceptionMessages.int.dropped-negative: Both numbers are negative, so the answer is negative too. Moving left twice keeps you left of 0.
misconceptionMessages.int.subtracted-sizes: Both numbers are negative, so they don't cancel: add the sizes and keep the negative sign.
misconceptionMessages.int.wrong-sign: The size is right, but check the sign: use the sign of the number with the bigger size.
misconceptionMessages.int.added-sizes: The signs are different, so the numbers partly cancel: subtract the sizes instead of adding them.
misconceptionMessages.int.sub-ignored-sign: Watch the second number's sign. Subtracting means adding the opposite: change − to + and change the sign of the second number.
misconceptionMessages.int.sub-backwards: You can't swap the order in subtraction. A smaller number minus a bigger one: start at the first number and move left, past 0, so the answer is negative.
misconceptionMessages.int.wrong-sign-sub: The size is right, but check the sign. Rewrite it as adding the opposite, then use the sign rules.
